segments.text: What's inside a TV remote?
Let me explain.
Pop the back off:
a rubber keypad and a thin circuit board.
Flip a button over:
underneath sits a black pad of conductive carbon.
Press it,
and the pad bridges two gold tracks on the board.
The buttons are wired in a grid,
so one chip can tell which one you pressed.
But here's the trick:
at the front sits an LED you can't see.
It shines infrared light.
The chip flashes it 38,000 times a second,
segments.say: The chip flashes it thirty-eight thousand times a second,

segments.text: in bursts that spell a code.
Every button has its own pattern.
The TV's sensor only listens to that exact flicker,
so lamps and sunlight don't confuse it.
Want to see it?
Point the remote at your phone's selfie camera and press a button.
The camera sees the flash.
The first wireless TV remote, in 1955,
was basically a flashlight.
Next time:
what's inside a computer mouse?
